adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — dead comparison `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`: the find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy so it compares against undefined and never matches, causing `events.update` to be called with `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent`, the new expression:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

is logically broken: the `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it ends up searching for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`/"". That will not match a real destination calendar externalId, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`.

This is a regression from the previous behavior (`... : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) which correctly fell back to the event’s destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` was not provided. With the new code, `calendar.events.update` can be invoked without a valid `calendarId` (or will incorrectly fall back, depending on code outside the shown diff), so the finding identifies a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317 — same dead comparison in `deleteEvent`, so calendarId is always undefined without an explicit externalCalendarId and the delete falls back to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, 404ing and leaving orphaned events in non-primary destination calendars

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the new logic computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the else branch, `externalCalendarId` is falsy (otherwise the ternary would take the first branch), so the `.find()` predicate effectively compares each `cal.externalId === undefined/null`, which will not match a normal calendar externalId. That makes `calendarId` undefined whenever `externalCalendarId` isn’t explicitly provided, so deletion will target whatever fallback the method uses (the code even defines `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` immediately before), which can miss events created on non-primary destination calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credential for non-calendar references, so video booking references (Zoom, etc.) are written with `credentialId: undefined`, breaking later update/delete lookups

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the mapping that builds the booking reference object changed from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. This is a concrete behavioral change: for non-calendar integrations (e.g., video providers), even if `result.credentialId` exists, it will no longer be persisted into the reference. If the system later relies on `reference.credentialId` to select the correct integration credential (especially when multiple credentials of the same type exist), this will break update/delete resolution. The diff provides direct evidence of the credentialId being dropped for non-calendar references; the downstream breakage is a reasonable and likely consequence of that loss of data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:148-150 — selectedCalendar resolved solely by `cal.credentialId === credentialId` with `|| "primary"` fallback; since DestinationCalendar.credentialId is nullable and unset on legacy rows, those bookings are silently created in the user's primary calendar instead of the destination calendar

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now computed only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and if that returns undefined it falls back to `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). Because `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is treated as optional elsewhere in the diff (e.g., `if (destination.credentialId)` in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, and `destinationCalendar` is now an array), any destination calendar entry that has an `externalId` but lacks/misses the matching `credentialId` will not be selected and the event will be inserted into the user's primary calendar instead. This is a correctness regression compared to the old behavior which preferred `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly.

[]`, so a throw before calendarReference is assigned (e.g. in `prisma.booking.findFirst`) returns an empty array instead of a `success: false` result, and the removed `console.error(message)` makes the error completely silent

adjudication.rationale: In the shown diff, `calendarReference` is initialized as `PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined` before the `try`. If an exception is thrown before `calendarReference` is assigned (e.g., during the early DB reads like `prisma.booking.findFirst` / other awaited operations in the `try`), the `catch` now returns `Promise.resolve(calendarReference?.map(...) ?? ([] as Array<...>))`, which evaluates to `[]` when `calendarReference` is still `undefined`. Previously, the `catch` returned an array containing a single `{ success: false, ... }` result (and also did `console.error(message)`). The new code both (1) can hide failures by returning an empty array and (2) removed the only explicit logging in this catch path, making such failures silent in this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-Google calendar services ignore the new `credentialId` and always use `destinationCalendar[0]` (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73, larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156), so per-host createEvent calls for COLLECTIVE events all target the first host's externalId, producing duplicate writes/404s

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `CalendarManager.createEvent` does not pass that `externalId` into calendar providers; it only calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. GoogleCalendarService uses the passed `credentialId` to pick the matching calendar from `calEvent.destinationCalendar`, but the non-Google providers shown (Lark and Office365) still select the calendar via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`, i.e., always the first element. Therefore, when creating events per destination/host, Lark/Office365 will repeatedly target `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, causing duplicate inserts into the first host calendar and/or failures (e.g., 404/permission errors) when the credential used doesn’t have access to that first calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~440 — the recurring-event branch (already looping over every user calendar credential × updated booking) is now nested inside the new per-reference loop, so with N calendar references the same deletions are attempted N times, multiplying provider API calls and repeated 404/410s

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `bookingCalendarReference` from a single `.find(...)` result to an array via `.filter(...)`, and then wraps the deletion logic in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference) { ... }`. Inside that loop, when `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` is true, it runs `const promises = bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).map(async (credential) => { ... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) { ... calendar?.deleteEvent(...) } })` and then `await Promise.all(promises)`. That recurring deletion work is independent of `reference` (it iterates all user calendar credentials and all updated bookings), so if there are N calendar references, the same batch of deletions will be executed N times, multiplying provider API calls and likely causing repeated not-found responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 queries: `prisma.credential.findUnique` is issued inside per-destination/per-reference loops at packages/core/EventManager.ts:~345 and ~510 and handleCancelBooking.ts:~430; these should be a single `findMany({ where: { id: { in: [...] } } })` outside the loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/expands loops over destination calendars/references and performs `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside those loops when a credential isn’t already present in in-memory credentials. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, for each `destination` it may call `prisma.credential.findUnique` if `this.calendarCredentials` doesn’t contain it. In the updated `updateCalendarEvent` logic, it now loops over `calendarReference` and may call `prisma.credential.findUnique` per `reference` when `credential` is missing. In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, it now loops over `bookingCalendarReference` and may call `prisma.credential.findUnique` per reference if not found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`. This is a verifiable N+1 query/performance issue that could be reduced by batching with a single `findMany` outside the loops.
